about.dealer_change_ownership.reviews.bu: The new owner must provide CarGurus with a valid, executed purchase and sales agreement clearly indicating the prior ownership, the new ownership, and the date upon which the change occurred.

Dealer licences, lease agreements, state records or other documentation will not be accepted as evidence of an ownership change. The purchase and sale agreement may be redacted but the old/new owner data and date of ownership change must be present.
Reviews written prior to the provided notice of ownership change will display with a clear indication that the reviews were submitted under previous ownership.

Reviews submitted following the provided notice of ownership change will age out to zero impact on deal rating within a 6-month time frame from the date that valid notice was provided and accepted, with the greatest impact reduction occurring within 60 days

After 6 months, prior ownership reviews will no longer factor in to the aggregate star rating. Additionally, after 6 months, prior ownership reviews will be moved to the ‘Old reviews’ section in the VDP reviews widget and will continue to be clearly marked as reviews from the prior ownership, including any management responses.
New reviews have a greater weight, which will further help to accelerate mitigation of old reviews.

about.dealer_change_ownership.reviews.p1: It is our mission to provide the most accurate and trusted dealer reviews to our users. As such, in the event of a dealership change of ownership please follow the policy below to ensure a timely and transparent handling of reviews.
about.dealer_reviews.dealerships.bullets: We will NOT remove negative reviews simply because a dealer advertises with CarGurus.
Dealers must submit evidence to support any claim that a review is fraudulent.
A dealer's response will be published just below the review itself – make sure it is fit for public consumption and not aimed at the reviewer alone.
CarGurus strongly discourages dealers from asking customers to write reviews while still at the dealer’s or providing any financial incentive to a consumer for leaving a review.
Though they are still available to users, we do not include reviews older than {0} years when calculating a dealer''s overall rating.
about.dealer_reviews.dealerships.p1: Dealers who have an account with CarGurus will receive a notification shortly after a shopper submits a dealer review. That notification will include an invitation to respond to the review directly or challenge it as fraudulent. The tools to respond to reviews are available to any car dealer with stock on the site, regardless of whether it has a business relationship with CarGurus. Things to bear in mind:
about.dealer_reviews.how_dealer_reviews_: How do CarGurus' dealer reviews work?

CarGurus strongly believes in transparency in car shopping. We're confident any transaction between a car shopper and a dealer will be easier and pleasanter if that shopper and dealer communicate openly and honestly with each other before and after the transaction.

We let car shoppers publicly review dealers they've worked with while they're shopping for a car, and we allow dealers to respond to those reviews directly. In order to ensure high-quality reviews, we invite only those shoppers who have recently interacted with a dealer to review that dealer.
about.dealer_reviews.integrity.p1: CarGurus takes the integrity of our reviews very seriously and has a zero tolerance policy for fraudulent review submissions.  We have a variety of systems in place to monitor for and prevent fraud.
about.dealer_reviews.integrity.p2: Individuals who are determined to have submitted fraudulent reviews may have their ability to submit future reviews revoked. Dealers determined to have directly or indirectly participated in the submission of fraudulent reviews will be subject to warnings and, if repeated attempts at review fraud are detected, potential negative impact to their reputation on our site.
about.dealer_reviews.shoppers.bullets1: We want as many specifics as possible in reviews – saying a dealer is "Good" won't give other shoppers a very clear idea of how you felt about working with them.
about.dealer_reviews.shoppers.bullets2: We don't allow accusations of criminal conduct. If you think a dealer did something truly awful or illegal, please simply state the facts.
about.dealer_reviews.shoppers.bullets3: We don't allow profanity or any language that may be considered offensive in reviews.
about.dealer_reviews.shoppers.bullets5: We don't allow the use of last names in reviews.
about.dealer_reviews.shoppers.p1: Any car shopper who contacts a dealer about a listing via the CarGurus site will get up to two emails inviting them to review the dealer, starting about a week after that first contact. These invites will allow the shopper to rate the dealer overall with a star rating of 1 to 5 and to document his or her experience with that dealer.
about.dealer_reviews.shoppers.p2: If you plan to post a review, here are some things you should know:
about.dealer_reviews.shoppers.p3: Each dealer review CarGurus receives gets screened, and if we receive a review we can't publish for some reason, we invite the submitter to edit and re-submit it.

checkout.wizard.component.help.faq.finan: You can choose to pay either via finance or with cash. For finance (depending on your listing), you may be able to (1) apply for pre-qualified offers, (2) submit a full credit application or (3) estimate your monthly payments using the dealer's recommended APRs.

These are the two types of finance offers provided within the CarGurus car-buying experience (depending on your listing and pre-qualification status), and both are fully honoured at CarGurus' participating dealerships. While pre-qualified offers do not impact your credit score, submitting a full credit application saves more time at the dealership and may provide you with offers from more lenders.

Take your CarGurus finance offer to the dealership for the specific vehicle, and your dealer will be able to help you finalise your deal. If you don't have your offer with you, your dealer can still pull up your offer by entering your information into the dealer systems.
Yes, participating dealers have agreed to honour the finance terms you've received through CarGurus.
Your finance offer can only be applied to the specific vehicle you built the deal for. However, you can build deals and receive offers for as many vehicles as you would like on the CarGurus platform.
Everyone is welcome to see if they are able to receive offers with our participating lenders!

For pre-qualification finance, your credit score will not be impacted. If you submit a full credit application, your credit score will only be impacted for the initial application and will not be impacted within a 14-day period if you submit additional applications for multiple vehicles.

Throughout your car-buying experience, you may be able to receive additional offers via the different finance options available to you. If you explored all options and are unable to receive offers, your applications is likely still under review by our lending partners and will likely be waiting for you at the dealership. Reach out to the dealer for the up-to-date status!

corp.aboutus.v2.dealer.signup.body: Learn more about how CarGurus can help you reach local buyers.
corp.aboutus.v2.how.body1: Using proprietary technology, search algorithms and innovative data analytics, CarGurus provides unbiased insights into car pricing, dealer reputation and vehicle history.
corp.aboutus.v2.how.body2: For used vehicles, we calculate a fair retail price based on a detailed analysis of comparable current and previous car listings in a given market. We call this estimate the CarGurus Instant Market Value (IMV). Updated daily, CarGurus IMV takes into account millions of data points including make, model, variant, year, mileage, options, location and vehicle history.
corp.aboutus.v2.how.body3: To determine our deal ratings, we compare the asking price of a vehicle to the CarGurus IMV, and factor in dealer reputation. From this calculation, we rate the quality of the deal: Great, Good, Fair, High or Overpriced. We always sort organic search results with the best deals on top (based on our algorithm, not how much a dealer pays us).
corp.aboutus.v2.how.title: How we do it
corp.aboutus.v2.what.body: At CarGurus, we’re building the world’s most trusted and transparent automotive marketplace. We make it easy to find great deals from top-rated dealers and provide the guidance consumers need to make a more informed purchase. We also help dealers quickly and easily market their vehicles and connect with ready-to-buy shoppers.
corp.aboutus.v2.what.title: What we do
corp.aboutus.v2.who.body1: Founded in 2006 by Langley Steinert (co-founder of TripAdvisor), CarGurus is now the number one most visited online automotive marketplace in the US.*
corp.aboutus.v2.who.body2: CarGurus also operates sites in Canada and Germany, with other markets on the horizon. Our US offices are located in Cambridge, Massachusetts and Detroit, Michigan. Our international office is located in Dublin.
corp.aboutus.v2.who.body3: The company started trading on the Nasdaq in October, 2017 under the symbol CARG.

corp.team.bios.board.conines: Steve Conine is Co-Founder and Co-Chairman of Wayfair Inc, a leading global online destination for the home. Prior to co-founding Wayfair, Mr Conine served as Chief Technology Officer for Simplify Mobile Corporation, an enterprise software company he co-founded in 2001. He also served as Chief Operating Officer for the London office of iXL Enterprises, Inc. and Chief Technology Officer of Spinners Incorporated, an IT consulting company he co-founded. Mr Conine holds a Bachelor of Science from Cornell University.
corp.team.bios.board.gupta: Manik Gupta is Corporate Vice President, Microsoft Teams at Microsoft Corporation, a technology corporation. Prior to serving as Corporate Vice President, he served as Corporate Vice President, Microsoft Teams, Consumer Communications and Communities at Microsoft.  Prior to his work at Microsoft, he served as the Chief Product Officer at Uber Technologies, Inc., a transportation marketplace technology company.  He also serves as an advisor and investor to startups based in the US and India.  He holds an MBA in Analytical Finance and Strategic Marketing from the Indian School of Business, Hyderabad, India and a Bachelor of Applied Science in Computer Engineering from the Nanyang Technological University, Singapore.
corp.team.bios.board.haoy: Yvonne Hao is a Co-founder and has been a Managing Director of the private equity firm Cove Hill Partners since July 2019. Prior to that, she was the Chief Operating Officer and Chief Financial Officer of PillPack, where she was instrumental in that company's successful sale to and integration with Amazon. Prior to PillPack, Ms Hao spent almost nine years at Bain Capital, where she served as an Operating Partner and board member to several portfolio companies. Prior to Bain Capital, she held roles in Corporate Strategy and Global Marketing at Honeywell and worked at McKinsey, where she started her career and was promoted to Associate Partner. Ms Hao also serves on the board of directors of Flywire Corporation, a global payments enablement and software company. Ms Hao holds a BA from Williams College and a Master of Philosophy in Development Economics from Cambridge University.
corp.team.bios.board.hickokl.2: Lori Hickok most recently served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial and Development Officer for Scripps Networks Interactive, Inc., a leader in lifestyle media with brands including HGTV, Travel Channel and The Food Network. She also previously served as Scripps’ Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Executive Vice President, Finance. Ms Hickok first joined The EW. Scripps Company in 1988 and held positions as Vice President and Corporate Controller, Chief Analyst for Corporate Development, New Media Operations Controller and Divisional Controller. Ms Hickok also serves on the board of directors of 1stdibs.com, Inc., an online marketplace for luxury design products, as well as the Second Harvest Food Bank of East Tennessee and the YWCA Knoxville & the Tennessee Valley. A retired certified public accountant, Ms Hickok holds a Bachelor of Science in Accounting & Finance from Miami University.

credit_app.component.review.dropping_app:
Accept disclosures and notices
In order to apply online, you must review and agree to the application disclosures and consents below.
Summary:
• The information on this application, including any information you submitted previously, is correct.
• You authorise AutoFi to share your information and your application with the dealer, certain lenders that the dealer chooses and its service providers in order to help you apply for finance.
• You consent to electronic delivery of notices and disclosures
• When you submit this application, you authorise an enquiry into your credit history by the dealer and its finance partners, and you authorise the dealer to submit your credit application to its participating finance partners to help you apply for finance.

Credit application additional disclosures
For all applicants
• Everything that you have stated in this application, including any information you submitted previously, is true and correct.
• You are of legal age to enter a contract.
• You authorise the dealer and any finance company, bank or other financial institution to which the dealer submits your application (“Creditor” or “we” or “us” or “our”) to obtain your credit report and employment history in connection with this application, verify your income, and provide and/or obtain information about our credit experience with you.
• You must have physical damage insurance covering loss or damage to the vehicle for the term of any finance. You have the option to select an insurance agent or broker of your choice, whether affiliated with the Creditor or not. Your choice of insurance will not affect the credit approval process unless the insurance does not satisfy the finance requirements or the insurance company does not satisfy the reasonable standards of the Creditor.
•You agree that we, our affiliates, agents and service providers may monitor and record telephone calls regarding your account to assure the quality of our service or for other reasons. You also expressly consent and agree to us, our affiliates, agents and service providers using written, electronic or verbal means to contact you. This consent includes, but is not limited to, contact by manual calling methods, prerecorded or artificial voice messages, emails and/or automatic telephone dialling systems. You agree that we, our affiliates, agents and service providers may do so using any e-mail address or any telephone number you provide, now or in future, including a number for a mobile phone or other wireless device, regardless of whether you incur charges as a result.
•Important information about procedures for applying for opening a new account. To help the government fight the funding of terrorism and money laundering activities, the law requires all financial institutions to obtain, verify and record information that identifies each person who opens an account. What this means to you: When you apply for or open an account, we will ask for your name, address, date of birth and other information that will allow us to identify you
•If you receive and accept a finance offer, generally the dealer will be the initial creditor under the finance contract and the dealer’s finance partner will assume the contract as assignee. In certain auto purchases through Arkansas and Ohio dealers, your finance agreement may be directly with the finance partner.

For California applicants:
Married individuals may apply for separate accounts.

For Maine applicants:
If your credit application is approved and you finance the purchase of your motor vehicle through Creditor, you will be required to insure the vehicle against loss or damage. Creditor requires collision coverage and comprehensive coverage or fire and theft coverage. In addition, if this application is for a lease, Creditor will also require you to obtain liability insurance.

You have the option to select an agent or broker of your choice, whether or not affiliated with Creditor. Obtaining insurance from a particular agent or broker does not affect credit decisions by Creditor, unless the insurance product selected violates the terms of your contract for the purchase or lease of the motor vehicle.

For New Hampshire applicants:
If you are applying for a balloon payment contract, you are entitled, if you ask, to receive a written estimate of the monthly payment amount for refinancing the balloon payment in accordance with the creditor’s existing refinance programmes. You will be entitled to receive the estimate before you enter into the balloon payment contract. A balloon payment contract is an instalment sale contract with a final scheduled payment that is at least twice the amount of one of the earlier scheduled equal periodic instalment payments.

For New York applicants:
A consumer report may be requested in connection with your application for credit. Upon your request, we will tell you whether or not the consumer report was requested and give you the name and address of the consumer reporting agency that furnished the report. If your application is granted, subsequent consumer reports may be obtained in connection with any update, extension or renewal of credit.

For Ohio applicants:
The Ohio laws against discrimination require that all creditors make credit equally available to all creditworthy customers and that credit reporting agencies maintain separate credit histories on each individual upon request. The Ohio Civil Rights Commission administers compliance with this law.

For Rhode Island applicants:
Credit reports may be obtained in connection with your application.

For Tennessee applicants:
You must maintain insurance as described in the contract. You may purchase this insurance from anyone you choose. financing.calculator.landing.faqs.affect: What factors affect my loan payment and interest rate?
The total cost of the vehicle and your deposit will affect the total loan amount, whereas factors like your credit score will affect your interest rate.
financing.calculator.landing.faqs.afford: How do I know what I can afford?

As a rule of thumb, a new car payment should be no more than 15% of your monthly income, and a used car or lease payment should be no more than 10% of your monthly income. Your total monthly car expenses should not exceed 20% of your monthly take-home pay.
financing.calculator.landing.faqs.calcul: How do I calculate my total interest paid on a car loan?

Total interest = P (principal/total loan amount) * R (interest rate) * L (life of the loan)
• Ex.: a £25,000 5-year loan with a 5% interest rate would be 25,000 * 0.05 * 5 = £6,250.
Monthly interest = (interest rate / 12) * loan balance.
• Ex.: a £20,000 loan with a 6% interest rate would be (0.06 / 12) * 20,000, or 0.005 * 20,000 = £100.

The total interest paid on a car loan is calculated using an amortisation schedule formula, which can be a bit tricky to do manually. If you use our loan calculator, you can simply subtract the loan principal (vehicle price - deposit) from the total cost of the loan, which we calculate for you.

How do I calculate my monthly payment?

Your monthly car payment is calculated by the total loan amount (principal + interest) divided by the number of months in your loan term.
• Ex.: a £50,000 loan with a total of £5,000 paid in interest for a 60-month loan would be (20,000 + 5,000) / 60, or £416.67 per month.

financing.calculator.landing.faqs.debt_t: How do I calculate my debt-to-income ratio?
Your debt-to-income ratio (DTI) is calculated by summing the total of all your debts and dividing by your total income.

financing.calculator.landing.faqs.refina: Can I refinance a car loan?
Yes. Refinancing a loan is a common way to try to reduce the monthly payment or total interest paid on a car loan.
financing.calculator.landing.faqs.used_c: Are used cars’ interest rates higher?
On average, interest rates on a used car will be higher than that of a similarly priced new car.

How Pre-Qualification Works with CarGurus Participating Lenders
Obtain conditional pre-qualification for auto finance with a CarGurus Participating Lender (listed below) prior to visiting a participating dealer. Participating Lenders review the information you provide to determine whether you pre-qualify with no impact on your credit score. If you pre-qualify with one or more of our Participating Lenders, you will be able to see your monthly payments, APRs and offer summaries for vehicles you may be considering.

Remember, your pre-qualification can only be used for the purchase of one personal use vehicle. The offer summary will include an estimate of the finance terms (including deposit) you could qualify for when you apply for finance at the dealer. When you are ready to finance a vehicle, you can send your offer summary to a participating dealer to let them know you are conditionally pre-qualified for auto finance with a CarGurus Participating Lender. If you have recently applied for and funded another loan with a CarGurus Participating Lender, this might impact your eligibility for a new loan with this pre-qualification.

General disclosures regarding CarGurus finance pre-qualification

Monthly payment, APR and product terms
Monthly payment and annual percentage rate (APR) terms are not final until your finance is completed at a participating dealer. These terms are based on information you provide and might change if you update any information in the CarGurus finance experience or at the dealer.

Pre-qualification does not guarantee that you will receive finance or any particular finance terms, which are subject to change based on each CarGurus Participating Lender’s evaluation of your credit application submitted at the dealer and any required documents.

To prequalify, you must be at least 18 years old and have a valid street address within the contiguous United States or an APO/FPO address.

Using Your CarGurus finance pre-qualification at a dealer
When you visit a participating dealer, show them your offer summary for the vehicle you would like to finance. Sharing with the dealer will allow that dealer to access your pre-qualified terms and preferences, including vehicle information. (Sharing is not a mandatory step.) Then you will fill out a credit application and provide any information needed for review to complete your finance. A credit application at the dealer will result in one or more enquiries posted to your credit file. After negotiating purchase terms and receiving dealer credit approval, you will sign a contract with the dealer reflecting both your purchase and finance terms. Your purchase will result in a retail instalment contract with the dealer as the original creditor.

Amount financed restrictions
Your maximum amount financed may be based on income, key credit characteristics, the vehicle you are purchasing, the details of the finance deal and/or the specific dealership from which you purchase the vehicle. The amount financed may include the vehicle sales price, tax, title, licence fees, dealer fees and any optional products, like service contracts and/or extended warranties, that you choose to purchase from the dealer. See the “Additional disclosures for Participating Lenders” section below for additional restrictions.

APR
APR is the annual percentage rate. Advertised rates depend on the individual's credit and key finance characteristics, including but not limited to the amount financed, term, loan-to-value (LTV) ratio, deposit amount and vehicle characteristics. A representative example of payment terms is as follows: a £1,000 deposit, an amount financed of £21,000 with an APR of 10.00% and a term of 72 months would have a monthly payment of £389.04. Deposit may be required in order to complete your purchase; deposits vary depending on your credit approval. Estimated rates are subject to change without notice.

Representative APR is based on the individual's credit and key finance characteristics, including but not limited to the amount financed, term, the loan-to-value (LTV) ratio and vehicle mileage. Your actual APR will be based on your specific situation.

Dealer Participation Requirements
CarGurus Participating Lenders provide finance for new and used vehicles purchased from participating dealers and offer pre-qualification at participating dealers through dealer websites. The list of participating dealers is subject to change. CarGurus Participating Lenders may not offer finance for certain dealers, auto brokers or private party sellers. CarGurus Finance Prequalification programme does not offer finance for lease buyouts.

Vehicle Type Restrictions
Pre-qualification terms with CarGurus Participating Lenders can only be used at participating dealer locations in connection with the purchase of a new or used car, light truck, MPV or SUV intended for personal use. Certain CarGurus Participating Lenders do not offer finance for commercial vehicles, motorcycles, recreational vehicles (RVs), ATVs, boats, campervans, motorhomes, vehicles with a history of chronic malfunctions and/or manufacturer or dealer buyback (alternatively referred to as a “lemon”) branded title vehicles, lease buyouts, or vehicles without a vehicle registration number or title issued. CarGurus Participating Lenders may determine a vehicle to be commercial or otherwise ineligible based on the model and/or information provided to such Lenders. See the “Additional Disclosures for Participating Lenders” section below for additional restrictions.

Third-party Information and Additional Products
CarGurus Participating Lenders use third-party information, which is otherwise available, to enhance your auto finance experience. Third-party information includes, but is not limited to, part exchange values, car images, dealer reported mileage, the price, description and availability of optional products that may be able to be financed with the vehicle (e.g., service contracts, GAP and protection products), dealer-advertised price and car details. Please note that third parties, including participating dealers, provide this information and that CarGurus Participating Lenders do not make any express or implied representations or warranties with respect to the accuracy of the provided third-party information. You should verify the accuracy of any third-party information on your own. All trademarks are the property of their respective owners. Vehicle images may not be representative of the dealer-advertised vehicle. Cars are subject to prior sale and availability should be confirmed with the dealer. Dealer-advertised prices for vehicles and other additional products are subject to change without notice.

Dealer-advertised prices for vehicles and other optional products may be negotiable and may not include tax, title, licence and other fees charged by the dealer. Other fees may include, but are not limited to, document fees, dealer preparation fees and delivery charges. You should verify with the dealer what is included in the dealer-advertised price. You should also verify tax, title and licence fees with the dealer. Should you choose to purchase any additional products, including GAP, service contract and/or extended warranty, from a participating dealer, such charges may impact your finance terms. Those additional products may or may not be offered or sold by a CarGurus Participating Lender.

Privacy
CarGurus Participating Lenders may collect information about you when you submit a pre-qualification application on the CarGurus’ website. For complete information, see each CarGurus Participating Lender’s privacy statement at:

For Capital One, see www.capitalone.com/identity-protection/privacy
For Westlake Financial, see www.westlakefinancial.com/privacy-policy/

When you visit a participating dealer, show them your offer summary for the vehicle you would like to finance. How pre-qualification works with CarGurus Participating Lenders:
Obtain conditional pre-qualification for auto finance with a CarGurus Participating Lender (listed below) prior to visiting a participating dealer. Participating Lenders may review the information you provide to determine whether you pre-qualify with no impact on your credit score. If you pre-qualify with one or more of our Participating Lenders, you will be able to see your monthly payments, APRs and offer summaries for vehicles you may be considering. Your request for pre-qualification may not be submitted to all Participating Lenders.

Remember: your pre-qualification can only be used for the purchase of one personal-use vehicle. The offer summary will include an estimate of the finance terms (including deposit) you could qualify for when you apply for finance at the dealer. When you are ready to finance a vehicle, you can send your offer summary to a participating dealer to let them know you are conditionally pre-qualified for auto finance with a CarGurus Participating Lender. If you have recently applied for and funded another loan with a CarGurus Participating Lender, this might impact your eligibility for a new loan with this pre-qualification.

CarGurus Participating Lenders
• Capital One, www.capitalone.com/cars
• Chase, www.cargurus.co.uk
• Global Lending Services, www.glsllc.com
• Westlake Financial, www.westlakefinancial.com

General disclosures regarding CarGurus finance pre-qualification

Monthly payment, APR and product terms
Monthly payment and annual percentage rate (APR) terms are not final until your finance is completed at a participating dealer. These terms are based on information you provide and might change if you update any information in the CarGurus finance experience or at the dealer.

Pre-qualification does not guarantee that you will receive finance or any particular finance terms, which are subject to change based on each CarGurus Participating Lender’s evaluation of your credit application submitted at the dealer and any required documents.

To pre-qualify, you must be at least 18 years old and have a valid street address within the contiguous United States or an APO/FPO address.

Using your CarGurus finance pre-qualification at a dealer
When you visit a participating dealer, show them your offer summary for the vehicle you would like to finance. The participating dealer will access your pre-qualified terms and preferences, including vehicle information. (Sharing is not a mandatory step.) Then you will fill out a credit application and provide any information needed for review to complete your finance. A credit application at the dealer will result in one or more enquiries posted to your credit file. After negotiating purchase terms and receiving dealer credit approval, you will sign a contract with the dealer reflecting both your purchase and finance terms. Your purchase will result in a retail instalment contract with the dealer as the original creditor.

Amount financed restrictions
Your maximum amount financed may be based on income, key credit characteristics, the vehicle you are purchasing, the details of the finance deal and/or the specific dealership from which you purchase the vehicle. The amount financed may include the vehicle sales price, tax, title, licence fees, dealer fees and any optional products, like service contracts and/or extended warranties, that you choose to purchase from the dealer. See the “Additional disclosures for Participating Lenders” section below for additional restrictions.

APR
APR is the annual percentage rate. Advertised rates depend on the individual's credit and key finance characteristics, including but not limited to the amount financed, term, loan-to-value (LTV) ratio, deposit amount and vehicle characteristics. Deposit may be required in order to complete your purchase; deposits vary depending on your credit approval. Estimated rates are subject to change without notice.

Dealer participation requirements
CarGurus Participating Lenders provide finance for used vehicles purchased from participating dealers and offer pre-qualification at participating dealers through dealer websites. The list of participating dealers is subject to change. CarGurus Participating Lenders may not offer finance for certain dealers, auto brokers or private party sellers. CarGurus’ finance pre-qualification programme does not offer finance for lease buyouts.

Vehicle type restrictions
Pre-qualification terms with CarGurus Participating Lenders can only be used at participating dealer locations in connection with the purchase of a new or used car, light truck, MPV or SUV intended for personal use. Certain CarGurus Participating Lenders do not offer finance for commercial vehicles, motorcycles, recreational vehicles (RVs), ATVs, boats, campervans, motorhomes, vehicles with a history of chronic malfunctions and/or manufacturer or dealer buyback (alternatively referred to as a “lemon”) branded title vehicles, lease buyouts or vehicles without a vehicle registration number or title issued. CarGurus Participating Lenders may determine a vehicle to be commercial or otherwise ineligible based on the model and/or information provided to such Lenders. See the “Additional disclosures for Participating Lenders” section below for additional restrictions.

Third-party information and additional products
CarGurus Participating Lenders use third-party information, otherwise available, to enhance your auto finance experience. Third-party information includes, but is not limited to, part exchange values, car images, dealer reported mileage, the price, description and availability of optional products that may be able to be financed with the vehicle (e.g. service contracts, GAP and protection products), dealer-advertised price and car details. Please note that third parties, including participating dealers, provide this information and that CarGurus Participating Lenders do not make any express or implied representations or warranties with respect to the accuracy of the provided third-party information. You should verify the accuracy of any third-party information on your own. All trademarks are the property of their respective owners. Vehicle images may not be representative of the dealer-advertised vehicle. Cars are subject to prior sale and availability should be confirmed with the dealer. Dealer-advertised prices for vehicles and other additional products are subject to change without notice.

Dealer-advertised prices for vehicles and other optional products may be negotiable and may not include tax, registration, licence and other fees charged by the dealer. Other fees may include, but are not limited to, documentation fees, dealer preparation fees and delivery charges. You should verify with the dealer what is included in the dealer-advertised price. You should also verify tax, title and licence fees with the dealer. Should you choose to purchase any additional products, including GAP, service contract and/or extended warranty, from a participating dealer, such charges may impact your finance terms. Those additional products may or may not be offered or sold by a CarGurus Participating Lender.

Privacy
When you fill out your pre-qualification request, you are providing your information to CarGurus so that CarGurus can facilitate your request for pre-qualification from a CarGurus Participating Lender and so that CarGurus can provide estimated finance offers for select vehicles displayed on CarGurus’ website, for which you are pre-qualified. CarGurus will use and share the information you provide consistent with the written instructions you provide to CarGurus in your pre-qualification request and in accordance with its Privacy Statement, available at: https://www.cargurus.co.uk/Cars/privacyPolicy.html. Additionally, should you complete your pre-qualification request on the CarGurus website, CarGurus Participating Lenders may use the information you provide in order to determine whether you may be eligible to pre-qualify for finance from one or more CarGurus Participating Lenders and to send you important information about your pre-qualification request. For complete information, see each CarGurus Participating Lender’s privacy policies at:

• For Capital One, see www.capitalone.com/privacy
• For Chase, see www.cargurus.co.uk
• For Westlake Financial, see www.westlakefinancial.com/privacy-policy/
• For Global Lending Services, see www.glsllc.com/privacy-1/

Additional disclosures for Capital One

Applicant restrictions
• Minimum monthly income required is £1,500, depending on your credit qualifications.
• Any existing Capital One accounts must be in good standing (not over limit, overdue or delinquent).
• Pre-qualification terms expire 30 days from the date your pre-qualification request is received.

Amount financed restrictions
• For used vehicles, the minimum amount financed is £4,000

Vehicle type restrictions
• The vehicle must have fewer than 120,000 miles and its model year must be within the last 10 years. In some instances, an older model year or higher-mileage vehicle (up to 150,000 miles) may be eligible.

• Certain vehicle makes, including but not limited to, Oldsmobile, Daewoo, Saab, Suzuki or Isuzu are not eligible for finance.

Additional disclosures for Westlake Financial

Applicant restrictions
• Existing Westlake/Western Funding/Wilshire consumer credit accounts must be in good standing
• No open bankruptcies
• Maximum of one open derogatory account (not including collection accounts and student loan accounts)
• Open auto loans require further review, and in most cases must be traded in or paid off
• Out-of-state purchases are subject to review
• Customer address must be a permanent, non-commercial property

Amount financed restrictions
• Minimum amount financed is £4,000

Vehicle type restrictions
• Exotic makes (Ferrari, Maserati, Lamborghini, McLaren, etc.) ineligible
• Branded titles and commercial vehicles ineligible.

Additional disclosures for Global Lending Services

Applicant restrictions
• Applicant and co-applicant must be older than 18 years of age.
• Applicant or co-applicant’s primary source of income cannot be self-employment income or 1099 income.
• At least one applicant must have a gross monthly income of £1,800 or greater.
• Applicant(s) should have at least 2 years of job history with no employment gaps and a max of 2 jobs within the last 2 years.
• No open bankruptcies or recent major derogatories.
• A pre-qualification is valid for 30 days from the date the pre-qualification is granted.

Amount financed restrictions
• Minimum amount financed is £6,500

Vehicle type restrictions
• Vehicle must be less than 10 years old.
• Vehicle must have less than 122,000 miles
• Exotic makes, discontinued makes, smart cars, electric cars, grey market cars, modified cars, weather-damaged cars, branded-title cars, salvage-title cars, remanufactured-title cars, manufacturer "lemon law" buybacks, commercial vehicles, limousines, taxis, delivery vehicles, tow or heavy-duty vehicles and any vehicle not listed in NADA/KBB are ineligible for finance.

In the event that you have a problem with the vehicle, you can be confident that the manufacturer or dealer will often provide repairs free of charge or at a limited cost. Now you can shop for vehicles of high quality and rely on CarGurus' Instant Market Value to find the best CPO deal!

CarGurus Instant Market Value is the estimated fair retail price for a vehicle based on similar listings in the market. We analyse millions of data points to determine the CarGurus Instant Market Value for a vehicle based on year, vehicle condition, variant, mileage, gearbox, options, region and other factors.

sellmycar.faq.c2d.1.answer: When selling a vehicle, you have a few convenient options: getting the best offer, selling privately on CarGurus or bringing it to a car dealership. Getting an offer on CarGurus is a fast and convenient way to get a great value for your vehicle from the comfort of your home. Selling privately will give you the ability to connect with many interested buyers and the potential to make more. Part exchanging at a dealership is an option to sell your car for cash, though you could be selling it for less than what your car is worth.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.1.title: How can I sell my car?
sellmycar.faq.c2d.2.answer: First, you will be asked to provide the details and condition of your vehicle to receive an offer. If you accept this offer, we'll ask for a few documents to confirm your ownership of the vehicle. Next, schedule a pickup date that is within seven days of accepting the offer. On the scheduled date, your vehicle will be picked up and you will get paid! Terms and conditions apply.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.2.title: How does the offer process work?
sellmycar.faq.c2d.3.answer: Thousands of CarOffer dealers place orders for the vehicles they would like to purchase. CarOffer uses these orders to identify how much a dealer would pay for your vehicle and provides the best offer to you.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.3.title: How is my offer calculated?
sellmycar.faq.c2d.4.answer: CarOffer is a majority-owned subsidiary of CarGurus that leverages patented technology to enable dealers to buy and sell used vehicles instantly.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.4.title: Who is CarOffer?
sellmycar.faq.c2d.5.answer: Your offer will be valid for seven days or after driving 250 additional miles (whichever comes first).
sellmycar.faq.c2d.5.title: How long is my offer valid for?
sellmycar.faq.c2d.6.answer.p1: To receive your payment, we recommend linking your bank account through our secure portal. This will be the fastest and easiest way for you to receive your funds. If your bank isn't compatible with our system, we offer a cheque as an option, as well.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.6.answer.p2: If bank transfer is selected, payment will be received in 1–3 business days.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.6.answer.p3: If “cheque” is selected, then it will be delivered as early as the time of pickup. Please note that you will have to wait for confirmation of cheque activation before depositing. Additionally, some banks have deposit limits and may hold the funds for multiple days before they're deposited in your account.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.6.title: What are my payment options and when do I get paid?
sellmycar.faq.c2d.7.answer.p1: Some cars won’t be eligible for an offer. Reasons include extensive damage, high mileage, old age, exotic or rare models, non-drivable condition or no local interest.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.7.answer.p2: If your car has any of these issues, it's possible you won't get an offer. You can still list your car and we'll guide you through the process.

sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.1.answer: First, we’ll have you enter a few basic details about your car, like its make, model and mileage. If everything checks out, we’ll show an estimate value for your car (e.g. £7,000–£8,500) sourced from our trusted partners at Autozen. If you want to proceed, you’ll go to autozen.com, where you can schedule an inspection and confirm any remaining details. On pickup day, a driver will come get your car and you’ll get paid. No haggling. No obligation. No stress.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.1.title: How does the offer process work?
sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.2.answer.p1: When you sell your car with Autozen, you'll be presented with an Initial Estimated Value and an Autozen valuation.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.2.answer.p2: The Initial Estimated Value is based on the Canadian Black Book Value and additional data that is aggregated to come as close to a real market value as possible. This estimate does not take into consideration the accident history or condition of your vehicle. A range is provided to help with understanding the potential value; however, we encourage you to use it as a guide rather than a firm value. As you can imagine, the more we get to know your vehicle, the more likely it is that we can help determine your vehicle's unique value.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.2.answer.p3: Your Autozen Valuation that is finalised after inspection does indeed factor in your vehicle's accident and damage history. Every car is different, and we'll help you uncover the best price from multiple buyers that will compete for your vehicle!
sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.2.title: How do you value my car?
sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.3.answer.p1: Currently, we only accept vehicles from years 2010 and newer. If your vehicle is not listed even though it is newer, you can try to find it via another category. Please note that as this is a safe and secure payment method for a large one-off sum of money, so although they have officially transferred the funds to you, it may take 4-6 hours for your bank to process and deposit the money into your account. sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.6.answer.p1: Walkarounds help Autozen gather information about your vehicle so they can present it in the best light to buyers. During the walkaround, your certified Autozen expert will be reviewing your car, taking photos (inside and out) and taking a quick test drive.
sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.6.answer.p2: Walkarounds take roughly 30-40 minutes to complete, so you can relax while they do their thing!
sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.6.title: What happens during the walkaround inspection?
sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.7.answer.p1: All cars that are inspected before 5pm each day will be ready for the next available auction. Otherwise, it will simply be ready for the following one!
sellmycar.faq.c2d.ca.7.answer.p2: If you don’t get an offer straight away, there’s no need to worry! We’ve seen offers that come in on the first auction, or even the fourth or fifth. seo.contactless_option.landing_page_arti: Tips for buying a car during the COVID-19 pandemic
This will depend on the brand and model. Vehicles that are getting refreshed and are key to automotive companies’ profits are likely to hit the market. These include vehicles like the Fiat 500 Electric, the Alfa Romeo Tonale, the new Nissan Qashqai and the BMW 4 Series.

Vehicles that will get a minor update, such as the Audi Q5, may get pushed back to 2022. While there may be a model year 2021 vehicle, the timing cycle for minor product updates may get pushed back as both automotive companies and suppliers stop production. Automotive companies will do what they can to avoid delays. However, when plants shut down for 3–5 weeks, they can still stay on track for most model launches. However, if production delays extend for months, it may be harder to stay on track.

Car showrooms are allowed to open when there is no lockdown in place. When lockdowns are rolled out, you can still use online services to contact car dealerships, many of which are able to offer click and collect service or home delivery.

Breakdown cover services such as the AA and RAC are continuing to operate during the COVID-19 lockdown. Contact them either via their respective app or by phone in order to have your car recovered, bearing in mind that you’ll need to observe social distancing measures when they arrive. Garages and service workshops are also allowed to remain open, primarily in order to keep key workers moving. It should therefore still be possible to have your car repaired, assuming any necessary parts are available.

Many dealerships are offering new car delivery during the COVID-19 crisis. Any dealers offering this service should also clean the car at the point of handover and offer a full digital service for payment and signing of documents.

If you’re concerned your car might have come into contact with the novel coronavirus – for example, if a person with COVID-19 symptoms has travelled in it – you should disinfect it. This is important not only for your own well-being, but also to help prevent the spread of the novel coronavirus. For more information on how to disinfect a car, CarGurus has published a guide to cleaning your car to help prevent the spread of the novel coronavirus.

During those periods when the country is not in lockdown, car showrooms will be open and implementing social distancing measures to ensure buyers can shop safely. For those who would rather not look at a car in person, dealerships have staff available to chat over the phone or answer queries online. CarGurus has launched a range of search filters to make it easy to find dealerships that are offering these and other contactless services.
For more information, please see our guide to safely buying a car during the COVID-19 lockdown.

If your car finance is coming to an end during the COVID-19 crisis, you should contact your lender to find out what your options are. Have your contract details to hand to save time. It is also worth contacting the dealership that supplied the car in the first place – although showrooms are closed, many dealerships can still be contacted by phone or online. Depending on the type of finance agreement you have for your car, the options are likely to be similar to what they would be without the COVID-19 crisis. For a PCP (personal contract purchase), this means you can either return the car, buy it outright or swap it for a new one. If you want to buy the car outright, it is likely you’ll be able to do that without needing to visit the dealership.

Returning the car, or swapping it for a new one, will be more challenging during the lockdown. However, a dealership or your finance lender will be able to help you find a solution, such as extending your current contract until current restrictions are eased. Whatever option you settle on, bear in mind that it’ll need to be carried out online or over the phone.

If you carry a spare wheel in the car and you can stop in a safe place, this guide explains how to change a wheel yourself. You can then take the damaged tyre to a garage or service centre for repair or replacement. If you don’t have the option of changing the wheel yourself, breakdown cover services are still operating during the COVID-19 lockdown and will be able to help.

Options range from virtual appointments where you can speak to a sales representative over the phone or via a video call, right through to home deliveries or test drives from home. If you need to buy a car during the COVID-19 crisis, carry out your initial search online and then contact the dealers of the cars you are interested in to confirm what services they offer. To facilitate this process, CarGurus provides a series of search filters that allow you to see only cars from dealerships offering safer shopping measures.

Yes. Many showrooms offer click and collect purchasing or home delivery. While you’ll need to adhere to social distancing measures when visiting a car showroom, it is still perfectly possible to buy a car during the COVID-19 crisis.

Assuming you’re happy to buy online and accept that there might be a wait until you can collect or accept delivery of your car, there are some potential upsides to buying a car during the COVID-19 crisis. For example, interest rates are at the lowest level in history, which might mean you can find more compelling finance deals than would usually be offered.

Similarly, with people being on lockdown, demand for cars is also lower than usual. This might mean that there’s more flexibility in prices.

If your car lease is coming to an end while COVID-19 lockdowns are in place, you should contact the lease provider to discuss what your options are. It is unlikely that you will be able to physically return the car. However, it might be that the lease provider will extend the contract until lockdown restrictions ease – this might be a formal extension for a set amount of time or an informal rolling extension.

This depends on the person. If you are worried about being able to cover the monthly payment, leasing provides a great affordable option for consumers. However, with many automotive companies offering 0% for 84 months, there are great incentives in the new-vehicle market.

If a consumer needs to replace their vehicle and is concerned about their job security and financial well-being, a lease is a great option to keep monthly payments low. Consumers should also look at the used vehicle market. With used vehicle prices falling and vehicles sitting on dealer forecourts, consumers may find a Great Deal on a used vehicle that has already depreciated.

The most important point is to ensure that your car remains in roadworthy condition. Check to make sure the lights (including indicators), seatbelts and brakes all work, and look out for any warning lights on the dashboard after you’ve started the engine. You should also keep an eye on the oil and coolant levels and ensure the tyres haven’t developed any flat spots.
For more information, see our guide to basic car maintenance that you can carry out while the lockdown is in place.

No-contact car service, also known as contactless or concierge car service, is when a garage or shop collects and returns your car as part of its service or maintenance regime. Depending on where you live, the door-to-door nature of no-contact car service could mean you can still get your car maintained during the COVID-19 pandemic. It’s important to clean your car before it gets collected and when it is returned in order to help limit the spread of the novel coronavirus.

If you are worried about making a payment on your car loan or lease during the COVID-19 crisis, you should contact your lender at the earliest opportunity. A lender can’t offer help if it isn’t aware that a problem exists. Make sure you have your loan or lease contract available for reference when you contact your lender to save time.

Yes. The New England Journal of Medicine published a study in March 2020 that suggests that the novel coronavirus can survive on steel and plastic for up to 72 hours. In many countries, including the US, the UK, China and Italy, car manufacturing has been paused in an effort to slow the spread of the novel coronavirus. So even if a person with COVID-19 symptoms was working on an assembly line prior to a plant shutting down, that 72-hour window has easily passed by now.

If you’re using your car to carry out essential journeys, it is inevitable that you will need to fill it with fuel at some point. Petrol stations do remain open to facilitate this, but while visiting it’s important to follow guidance around social distancing and washing your hands (or using hand sanitiser). If available, use disposable gloves when picking up the petrol pump. Throw the gloves in the bin when you’re finished. Using a self-service payment pump can also help you comply with guidance around social distancing.

If you’re charging your car using an electric charger, it’s important to follow the same rules you would when filling up with petrol or diesel. So, wash your hands or use hand sanitiser before and after touching the car charging equipment, and wear a pair of disposable gloves if you have them, putting them in the bin when you’re finished.

Car owners have a number of options for selling their car themselves, but potential buyers may be uncomfortable dealing with the logistics of test driving and purchasing a car during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using CarGurus Pay will put your listing in front of an audience of verified buyers, provide assistance with paperwork and allow secure payment online. If you do sell your car during the COVID-19 crisis, it’s important to clean it to help minimise the spread of the novel coronavirus before handing it off to its new owner.

In theory, you can sell your car during the COVID-19 crisis. However, in practice, the rules around staying at home and social distancing could make it more difficult than usual. Bear in mind that during a lockdown it won’t be possible for somebody to come and collect your car.
Car service and MOT centres are open in order to carry out repairs and services, as well as MOT tests.

It is possible that some vehicles are harder to find because of stoppage in production. However, the decline in vehicle sales has resulted in higher vehicle supply levels. The industry data on vehicle supply shows stock levels increasing between February and March. After the country reopens, there could be a supply interruption as production ramps up and sales increase. But it is unlikely that there will be a shortage of popular luxury or non-luxury vehicles.

Similar to the domestic vehicles, it is possible that some vehicles are harder to find because of stoppage in production. However, for popular vehicles from brands like Nissan, Toyota and Honda, consumers should be able to find the vehicles they want. Vehicles that are being shipped may see a slight interruption in supply once sales rebound. But based on current stock and sales levels, it does not appear that there will be a major supply issue with imported vehicles.

Yes, your car does still need to be taxed during the COVID-19 crisis – you can renew your car tax online. If you’re not using your car at all and it is kept off the road you might consider making a Statutory Off Road Notification (SORN). You’ll get a refund for any full months of remaining tax, but you won’t be able to drive the car until you tax it again.

Many, but not all, dealerships are offering home test drives during the COVID-19 crisis. In this scenario, a sales representative would bring the car to a customer’s house (within a set distance from the dealership), disinfect it and then allow a solo test drive to take place. On completion of the test drive, the car is disinfected once again and taken back to the dealership. If the customer decides to go ahead with the purchase, all signing of paperwork and exchanging of funds can be carried out online. CarGurus makes it easy for car shoppers to find dealerships offering home test drives – simply select the relevant search filter when carrying out your search.
Letting any car sit still for a long time can lead to issues with the batteries, brakes and tyres.

Batteries can be drained even when the car is switched off if electrical items remain active (alarms, for example). At worst, this could mean your car will fail to start just at the moment you need it. If your car is parked on property you own, you can overcome this danger by plugging in to a “trickle charger”, which keeps the battery charged via a conventional wall socket. Failing that, you should start your car and run it for 15 to 20 minutes once a week or so. That will top off the battery as well as circulate fluids around the engine. Running the air conditioning at the same time will help prevent mould from developing within your system.

When a car’s brakes aren’t used for a prolonged period, they can begin to rust on the surface. This in turn can make them noisy and cause them to seize. To prevent this from happening, roll the car backward and forward a few times. If you’re parked on private land and it’s flat, you can also leave the emergency brake off to prevent it from seizing. Be sure to leave the car in gear to prevent it from moving.
By rolling your car a few metres, you can help prevent the tyres from developing flat spots.

seo.electric.faq.best_range.answer: If you go by official figures, the Tesla Model S is currently the electric car with the longest range from a single charge. The long-range model has an official range of 405 miles. The real-world range is likely to be less than that, and as with a petrol or diesel car will depend on driving style.

seo.electric.faq.charging_cost.answer.wi: The cost of charging an electric car depends on a number of factors and can vary greatly. For a start, the larger the battery in your car, the more it’ll cost to fill it with electricity (just as a big petrol tank will cost more to fill than a small one). The charging cost also depends on where and how you charge. The cheapest way to charge is via a home wallbox. These cost from under £400 to buy and install, after which you just pay the cost of electricity. This will vary depending on your tariff, but the average cost of electricity in the UK is around 15p/kWh. Based on this, a full charge for an early electric car will be around £3, while you’ll pay around £10 for a newer model such as the Kia e-Niro. For a more detailed breakdown, including the costs of using public chargers, see our guide to the cost of charging an electric car.

seo.electric.faq.gearbox.answer: No, electric cars do not need gears in the same way as a conventional petrol or diesel engine does. Instead they have a single forward gear (generally called drive) and can also switch to reverse or neutral. The reason electric cars do not need conventional gearboxes is because they are efficient throughout their whole rev range rather than needing to sit at a particular RPM to be efficient. Electric motors also deliver maximum torque from very low RPM and can spin at up to 20,000 RPM, whereas even a high-revving petrol engine will be limited to a maximum of around 8,000 RPM and a diesel to 5,000 RPM.
seo.electric.faq.gearbox.question: Do electric cars need gears?
seo.electric.faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
seo.electric.faq.is_it_magic.answer: Put simply, electric cars feature three core components to make them work: a motor, a battery and a control unit. The battery is where the electricity is stored – the larger it is, the further you’ll be able to travel between charges. The motor is what drives the wheels of an electric car (you can have one or more depending on the car). And the control unit is what sends the power between the battery and the motor. In addition to these core features, an electric car can recover energy when you slow down to feed back into the battery. This process is known as regenerative braking and in cars such as the BMW i3 can be so powerful that you can do much of your driving without having to use the brake pedal.
seo.electric.faq.is_it_magic.question: How do electric cars work?
seo.electric.faq.save_the_earth.answer.n: There is increasing evidence that electric cars are better for the environment based on the lifetime emissions of an electric vehicle versus those of a petrol or diesel model. At an obvious level, electric cars improve local air quality by not emitting any tailpipe emissions. However, the electricity to power them still has to come from somewhere, which sometimes means power stations that burn coal. In that scenario, emissions are merely offset rather than eradicated. However, as electricity production moves increasingly towards renewable sources, the overall environmental impact of electric cars is decreasing.  It’s a similar story when it comes to the production of electric cars, and their batteries in particular: as more renewable energy is used to make the batteries, so the environmental impact is reduced. That’s not to say electric cars are perfect – they still emit the same kinds of tyre and brake particles as other cars, for example – but on balance there’s a growing acceptance that they are better for the environment.

seo.electric.faq.time_to_charge.answer: There are a number of factors that determine the charging time for an electric car. First is the size of the battery; the bigger it is, the longer it’ll take to charge. Next comes the speed of the charger that you’re using. The slowest ways to charge are with a three-pin domestic plug or a 3kW wallbox, both of which are going to be overnight jobs, even for electric cars with small batteries. Using a fast charger (rated at 7kW to 22kW) will cut that time to around three hours for an early electric car with a small battery, or around 6–8 hours for a long range electric car. Public rapid chargers and ultra rapid chargers are much quicker and can offer a boost of around 80% to your car’s battery in around 30 minutes to an hour. But that’s only if your car is compatible with the high charging speeds that rapid chargers are capable of. For more details read our full guide on how to charge an electric car.
seo.electric.faq.time_to_charge.question: How long does it take to charge an electric car?
seo.electric.faq.whats_best.answer: The Tesla Model 3 might well fit many peoples’ definition of the “best” electric car. However, as with any type of car, the best model for you is the one that is going to most easily fit with your requirements. For some, that requirement might be low purchase price, in which case an early Nissan Leaf or Renault Zoe is worth considering. For others it’ll be the range from a single charge, for which models such as the Tesla, Kia e-Niro and Nissan Leaf e+ are easy to recommend. Then there are the high-performance electric cars, such as the Porsche Taycan and top models of Tesla, which fulfil a different brief and are arguably best from a technological point of view. The point is that the choice of electric cars on the used market has expanded so rapidly in the past couple of years that there are now models to suit most requirements. For a more detailed roundup, visit our guide to the most exciting electric cars due to arrive in 2021.
seo.electric.faq.whats_best.question: What is the best electric car?
seo.electric.faq.whats_cheapest.answer: As a used purchase, an early Nissan Leaf will be among the cheapest electric cars to buy. Bear in mind that early examples of the Leaf didn’t have a huge range from a single charge when new. Factor in some battery degradation now that the cars are a few years old and you might find that an early Leaf can now only travel around 40 or 50 miles between charges. For some people that will still make it a perfectly viable option, but if you regularly undertake longer journeys, it’ll likely be worth it to spend more to get a car with a longer range from a charge. With some early examples of the Leaf (and many examples of the first generation Renault Zoe), the battery will be leased rather than included with the car’s purchase price. As a result, you’ll need to factor in monthly battery payments (of around £50 and upwards depending on mileage) on top of the purchase price.

seo.gm_cpo_landing.header.subheading: What does approved used mean? It’s the final product after a rigorous process to ensure that cars are in good shape and well maintained. Approved used vehicles provide that extra dose of confidence, and they often include a long list of great benefits you won’t get with a typical used car, truck or SUV. When you buy a Chevrolet, Buick or GMC approved used vehicle, you’ll have peace of mind knowing that each and every vehicle is less than six years old, has fewer than 75,000 miles, has passed an extensive selection process and comes with many amazing benefits.
seo.gm_cpo_landing.info_section.bullet_1: All vehicles must be less than six years old and have fewer than 75,000 miles.
seo.gm_cpo_landing.info_section.bullet_2: All vehicles have a 12-month/12,000-mile “bumper-to-bumper” limited warranty<sup>1</sup> and a six-year/100,000-mile powertrain limited warranty<sup>2</sup>, both with £0 excess.
All vehicles have a 12-month/12,000-mile "Bumper to Bumper" Limited Warranty and a 6-year/100,000-mile Powertrain Limited Warranty, both with a $0 deductible.
seo.gm_cpo_landing.info_section.bullet_3: Be confident knowing that GM has your back and won't leave you stranded if something does happen to your vehicle.
seo.gm_cpo_landing.info_section.bullet_4: Every vehicle comes with two scheduled maintenance visits to use within the first two years/24,000 miles<sup>4</sup> of ownership to help ensure everything’s running smoothly.
Every vehicle comes with two scheduled maintenance visits for owners to use within the first two years or 24,000 miles of ownership, just in case.
seo.gm_cpo_landing.info_section.bullet_5: A three-day/150-mile<sup>5</sup> policy gives you extra reassurance in case you change your mind.
GM offers a three-day/150-mile exchange policy on every approved vehicle so you can feel more confident in your purchase.
seo.gm_cpo_landing.info_section.bullet_6: Every approved vehicle comes with a free vehicle history report so that owners can know everything that's happened to their car prior to purchase.
seo.gm_cpo_landing.info_section.bullet_7: Before an approved used vehicle is listed or sold, GM requires dealers to complete all safety recalls. However, because even the best processes can break down, we encourage you to check the recall status of any vehicle at my.gm.com/recalls and www.gov.uk/check-vehicle-recall.

All vehicles undergo a thorough inspection and reconditioning process to earn GM's "approved" badge. That means any vehicles with issues are either fixed or removed from the programme. Reliability and safety are GM approved used top priorities.
seo.gm_cpo_landing.info_section.bullet_8: Before an approved used vehicle is listed or sold, GM requires dealers to complete all safety recalls. However, shoppers are always encouraged to check the recall status of any vehicle themselves at www.gov.uk/check-vehicle-recall.
